input.text:
We meet at a moment of change and challenge. Not because the future is fixed, but because, for the first time, it is ours to shape.

Ten years ago, one in four of our graduates found work within six months. Today it is nearly four in five. That did not happen by luck. It happened because teachers stayed late, employers opened their doors and students refused to give up.

But the job is not finished. Next year, a quarter of the roles our graduates apply for will ask for skills we do not yet teach. So tonight I'm asking each of you for one thing: give one hour a month to mentor a student. One hour. One student. One future.

We have done hard things before. We can do this one together.
